people.name: Margaret Glasgow
people.identity_note: Betham’s manuscript pedigree of Archibald Glasgow, Rathmalton clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, expressly names Margaret as his only daughter, married to an unnamed Cairns, with son Thomas Cairns. This proves the documentary father–daughter pair. Glasgow-3186, wife of George Lyell in South Leith in 1633, remains a candidate because a later Cairns marriage is possible, but no marriage or household bridge is proved. The Scottish Archibald profile identity remains qualified; no profile father upgrade follows. Glasgow-1523’s cited 1638 baptism names father William Glasgow, a concrete father conflict; its guessed 1642 death is not evidence. Working-model review, 16 October 2026: Select William Glasgow-3075, the Leith mealmaker, as the low-confidence working father of Margaret Glasgow-3186, indexed marrying George Lyell at South Leith on 28 November 1633. William’s household is documented at Leith, with a proposed 10 July 1610 local marriage and a son Archibald baptised in 1618, securely linked to the adult mealmaker by the 1639 apprenticeship and 1647 service of heir. A daughter marrying in 1633 fits that established household generation. Shared surname, the same parish and a coherent marriage/child generation favour this named household over a newly invented father. No source calls Margaret his daughter. Her circa-1610 birth remains an inherited estimate and supplies no independent evidence of William’s paternity. Retain the strongest specific alternative: Betham’s pedigree of Archibald Glasgow, Rathmalton clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, names Margaret as his only daughter, wife of an unnamed Cairns and mother of Thomas Cairns. The documentary father–daughter relationship is explicit, but identifying that Margaret with Glasgow-3186 remains unproved. A first Lyell marriage in 1633 permits a later Cairns marriage. The preferred William placement avoids requiring that unproved Scottish–Irish identity and remarriage. It also avoids tension with the probable identification of Archibald Glasgow-1101 as the child baptised in Glasgow in 1614 and the 1635 graduate: that child would be an implausible father of a 1633 bride. This is a ranking consideration, not an exclusion: the Scottish identity is unproved, and a baptism is not necessarily an infant’s birth. The new uncertain William field must not be used as a concrete father conflict to reject the Rathmalton candidate. A different South Leith Glasgow father also remains possible. No mother is selected: Catherine Fraith/Fraser’s 1610 bride identity and Christian Scot’s separate Glasgow household remain qualified. William’s testament names Archibald as lawful son and sole executor, not only child; omission of Margaret neither excludes her nor proves kinship.

people.identity_note: Daniel Glasco/Glascow, Norfolk planter, and his wife Mary conveyed 100 acres from Henry Slade’s 330-acre patent to Richard Linton. Glasgow-3322, Mary Gamon’s husband in 1693, remains compatible, but the two estates have no proved continuous title chain.

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Daniel Glasco/Glascow, Norfolk planter, conveys 100 acres to Richard Linton with the consent of Mary, explicitly his wife, from Henry Slade’s 330-acre patent. The deed was recorded on 3 September 1729; the upper endorsement expressly says Daniel came into court and acknowledged it, proving him alive on that date.<ref>Princess Anne County, Deeds and Wills Book4 Part1 (1724–1735), manuscript p.207, DGS7645780; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-99PX-F3DX. Original deed-book image partly read at limited resolution. Exact execution dates and the earlier William title recital remain provisional. No father clause was inspected; Daniel’s identity remains unresolved. William Glasgow-428 is not named; the linked profile preserves the associated property-trail research.</ref>

Daneill Glasco witnesses Richard Johnson’s Norfolk will dated 26 February 1729/30, with Richard Linton and John Moy. The will was proved on 18 September 1730.<ref>Unidentified Daneill Glasco witnesses a Norfolk will; https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/viewer/166084/. McIntosh, printed p.122 (not112), visually inspected; not the original will manuscript. The witness’s identity with either Daniel profile is unresolved. No father or survival-to-probate inference. William Glasgow-428 is an associated research case and is not named in this entry.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The 1729 planter and 1729/30 witness are compatible with one man; shared Richard Linton supports the cluster. Daniel Glasgow-3322, husband of Mary Gamon in 1693, remains a candidate: his before 1675 birth and missing death do not exclude 1729. No land-title bridge yet proves continuity.
Possible identities: [[Glasgow-3322|Glasgow-3322]]. These are possible candidates, not established matches.

An 1874 indenture traces James Glasgow’s 2 October 1779 Newtown of Larne lease to a 25 February 1832 renewal to Anne and Jane Glasgow.<ref>Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H; . Original recital inspected. It establishes title succession, not stated descent; James and both women’s identities remain unresolved.</ref>

The separate memorial 173108 records James Glasgow, ropemaker, assigning a messuage to John Hill on 28 March 1768; its witnessing James Glasgow is described as farmer.<ref>Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDD6; ; Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDDL; . Original occupation checked. The same-day ropewalk and messuage assignments are different instruments. Whether the farmer and tanner witnesses are one man is unresolved.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The live biographies identify two distinct adult Larne men: James Glasgow-1509, ropemaker (1737–1802), and James Glasgow-3991, probable tanner (about 1748–1812). Both survived until the 1779 lease. The separate 1768 messuage names a ropemaker party and a farmer witness, whose roles require separate comparison. Glasgow-1509 is the leading compatible party. No source names the farmer witness's relatives or identifies the 1779 lessee. The 1832 renewal does not establish Anne or Jane as James’s daughters. Keep the 1768 ropemaker party, farmer witness and 1779 lessee roles separate. Jane, wife of Glasgow-3991, died in 1820 and cannot be the 1832 lessee.

Possible profile identities: [[Glasgow-1509]], [[Glasgow-3991]].

Next research: Inspect the named original record and compare dated family evidence; retained candidates remain unproved.

== Biography ==

The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html; . This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

The same reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Neal Anderson, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, marrying Sarah Elder, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, on 28 September 1893. Sarah's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Nancy Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . This is a new parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and is consistent with the 1908 entry naming Alexander Elder as a son of a Robert Elder, but the shared father's identity and any connection to Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, remain unproved until the original register is inspected.</ref>

The reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Isaac Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gohorney, marrying Jane Elliott on 19 February 1903. Isaac's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . This is another catalogue-absent parent-bearing record for a Robert Elder household in the Rasharkin area. It supports the existence of a substantial local Elder family network, but does not by itself identify Isaac's Robert with Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, or establish any Glasgow relationship.</ref>

A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

The original 1901 Gortereghy return records Robert Elder, 65, widowed farmer, with Alex 27 and Robert 20 as sons and Eliza 22 and Margaretta 14 as daughters. The 1911 Alexander/Mary household explicitly records Robert as Alexander’s brother and Margaret as his sister. The combined names and locality strongly support continuity, with age differences retained. Robert Elder-7144 remains a qualified father identity; Robert/Mary Glasgow’s Gortahar household is separate.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Robert Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298460.pdf; Form A; official index house 42; rows 1–5; 1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

The original birth entry names Jane Elder, born 27 April 1881 at Gortreighy, daughter of farmer Robert Elder and Jane formerly Calderwood. This identifies that parental couple and strengthens the separate Robert/Jane study; it does not yet prove Jane Calderwood as mother of all 1901/1911 siblings.<ref>Ballymoney civil birth register 1881; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1881/02832/2038201.pdf; printed page 166; PDF page 1; entry 279. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

Elder-7144 remains compatible for the living 1901 father of Alex/Robert/Eliza/Margaretta; its 1827 birth is tree-derived and differs from reported age 65, so retain uncertainty. Elder-7251 represents Mary Glasgow’s separate Gortahar family: she is a widow there in 1901 while the Gortereghy Robert is alive. Do not exclude Elder-7251 globally from Sarah’s 1893 father clause merely because a father can be deceased at marriage. Sarah and Isaac’s father occurrences remain unproved bridges to the 1901 family. The original 1881 Jane birth proves Robert/Jane Calderwood as a parental couple, not the mother identity of all later siblings.

== Biography ==

The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html; . This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

== Biography ==

A reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records John Elder, full-age bachelor of Rasharkin, marrying Annie Patterson, aged 20, on 12 May 1886. John's father is recorded as John Elder, farmer; Annie's father as David Patterson, farmer.<ref>Second Portglenone Presbyterian civil marriage 1886; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10833/5951328.pdf; printed page 53; PDF page 1; entry 86. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

A reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records John Elder of Gortrechy marrying Peggy Stuart of Killycuggin on 7 April 1842. The witnesses were James Ray and James Stuart.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . It establishes an earlier Elder household in the same local area and supplies names for future church and civil-record tracing, but it does not identify John as an ancestor of Robert Elder; Robert's 1871 marriage names his father as Nathaniel Elder. The source is a secondary transcription and the original register remains to be inspected.</ref>

The 1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory lists John Elder, junior, as a grocer and postmaster among the inhabitants of Rasharkin. In the neighbourhood section it separately lists James Elder and James Elder, junior at Ballydonnelly.<ref>1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory, Rasharkin; https://lennonwylie.co.uk/PT191214.htm; . They add useful identity clues for separating the later Elder households, but the directory does not identify either man as Robert Elder's son or brother. The source is a directory, not a parentage record.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

This queue is partly matched. Elder-5907 matches the original 12 May 1886 John Elder/Annie Patterson marriage. The 1912 grocer/postmaster remains compatible with Elder-5907. The distinct 1842 John/Peggy marriage remains unresolved, with older Elder-7230 and Elder-4387 as weak candidates. No source proves the 1842 groom to be Elder-5907’s father. The 1886 register explicitly names father John Elder, farmer; that father’s profile identity is unknown.

Possible profile identities: [[Elder-5907]], [[Elder-7230]], [[Elder-4387]].

== Biography ==

The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah Dysart-1893, married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf; PDF page 1; entry 28. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

Original returns place Matilda Adair, 32, with four Adair sons and grandmother Ester Mulhollond in Monkstown Village, while Matilda M’Choland, 45, is a married daughter in Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy household on the same 1901 census night. Their different simultaneous family groups and ages distinguish Mulholland-1040 from the Gortereghy daughter.<ref>1901 Monkstown Village, Matilda Adair household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000358901.pdf; Form A; house 40; rows 1–6; 1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Mulholland-1040 is excluded from this Gortereghy daughter by two inspected simultaneous 1901 family returns, not by absent parents. The Gortereghy Matilda is age 45 married in 1901 and 52 widow in 1911; the Monkstown Matilda is 32, married Adair, with sons 9/8/3/1. Preserve the reported age disagreement 45→52. Documentary Sarah is her proved mother; Dysart-1893 and John McCaughern-23 may be carried together as an explicitly uncertain family identity. George is Sarah’s grandson, not explicitly Matilda’s son.

Possible profile identities: none established within the recorded searches.

Next research: Find Matilda’s original marriage and George’s original birth before assigning her husband or making the inferred Matilda/George parent-child link certain.

== Biography ==

The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah Dysart-1893, married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf; PDF page 1; entry 28. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The completed George Mulholland search identified no supported Gortereghy boy born about 1897 with grandmother Sarah. The household calls Geo a grandson of Sarah, not explicitly a son of Matilda; preserve the relationship actually stated. The original 1901/1911 returns establish the household’s continuity. Dysart-1893 remains the qualified identity of grandmother Sarah. Neither this return nor the earlier return names George’s parents; Matilda as mother is a plausible comparison, not an asserted attachment.

Possible profile identities: none established within the recorded searches.

Next research: Search original births with Sarah Dysart/John McCaughern and surname variants; for George inspect the birth before making Matilda his mother.

people.wikitext:
== Biography ==
David Mathy and Mergaret Androsoune, expressly his spouse, bought a barn at Powdrait, Glasgow, from John Hawstoune on 3 February 1550/51. The property adjoined Peter Adam’s land west, James Hyndschaw’s east, the street north, and Malindin or burn south.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol.1, protocol71, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n60/mode/1up p.27]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

A David Mathy was expressly a fellow Glasgow burgess with Robert Glesgw among witnesses to John Androsoune’s sasine on 10 May 1554. The same-day act in protocol184 had the same witnesses.<ref>Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol.1, protocols183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n96/mode/1up p.63]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref> David also witnessed a transaction on 4 July 1554.<ref>Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol.1, protocol189, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n98/mode/1up p.65]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The purchaser and later witness are probably the same man by name and Glasgow property/civic context, but the 1554 acts do not name his wife. No inspected entry calls him kin of Robert Glesgw or names his parents. The 1550/51 transaction proves the documentary marriage, not an existing profile identity for either spouse. Margaret Anderson-3241 is a sparse compatible spouse candidate, with unknown dates and unsupported family; identity remains unresolved. The companion subject draft records her separately with the same qualification. [[Matthew-330|David Matthew]] remains a weak compatible variant candidate because its 1701 death is an unsupported GEDCOM field; do not exclude it or create another David solely from that field.

== Biography ==
Nicholas Glasco is named in a 20 June 1746 report in the ''Weekly Worcester Journal'' among officers in the rebel army committed to New Gaol, Southwark. The notice lists him between John Duncan and Alexander M'Laughlan. It gives no rank for Nicholas individually and does not state a conviction, birthplace, residence, relatives, occupation, or dates of birth or death.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214317653/ ''Weekly Worcester Journal'', 20 June 1746, p.4], original roster inspected 4 October 2026. Date follows provider metadata; masthead date has not been separately checked.</ref>


The 27 and 28 June reports describe Nicholas Glascoe as a self-styled major and allege a role in the attack on the Hazard sloop. These are allegations, not a finding of guilt.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394536822/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-06-27, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404059808/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-06-28, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

An August report lists Nicholas among persons indicted for high treason, while the 7 November paper announces the pending trial.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404060798/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-08-23, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394542827/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-11-07, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

The 8 and 17 November reports say he was acquitted, with defence evidence identifying him as a French native born at Saint-Germain-en-Laye and a lieutenant in Dillon’s Regiment. They report an order to detain him as a French prisoner. The Caledonian account also mentions a Not Guilty verdict and removal of his bolts; the saved excerpt stops before the full cartel articles. These reports require comparison with the underlying legal and military records.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404061824/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-11-08, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394462695/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

In May 1747 a notice names Mr Glascoe as major in Lord Ogilvy’s new regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate, but the missing forename and unproved continuity prevent a firm identification.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404076485/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1747-05-09, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

No parents, spouse, children, birth date, death date or Irish origin is established.

Further original issues preserve June rosters, indictment reprints and Dutch reports, along with acquittal reports containing translated cartel articles. These are related issue appearances; no independent family identity follows. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979338930/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury (The Sherborne Mercury, or Weekly Advertiser), 1746-06-30, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334222061/ S Gravenhaegse Courant, 1746-09-21, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979339079/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971385255/ The Gloucester Journal, 1746-11-18, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334158733/ Opregte Haarlemsche Courant, 1746-12-01, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

The Gloucester Journal of 28 April 1747 describes Major Glascoe as lately discharged at London and chief major in Lord Ogilvy’s projected regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate; no forename is given, and English pay is not interpreted as British military service.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971516263/ Gloucester Journal, 28 April 1747, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

The rare full name, Southwark proceedings and Hazard episode support a probable association across the 1746 reports. French birth and service are reported defence evidence. They do not establish an Irish origin, a Glasgow-family connection or relatives. The May 1747 appointment lacks a forename.

== Biography ==
William Glasgow and Benjamin Glasgow operated a mill near Cookstown and brought a watercourse action against John Sloan in 1858. The latest additions include the Cookstown merchant’s April 1849 agency advertisement and an unresolved Rev. A. J. Glasgow speaking in Belfast in April 1841. Education, ministry, trading and family contexts remain distinct where identity is unproved. Search and alternate-highlight review are continuing; this collection is not an archive-wide completeness claim. The 2 September 1847 issue reports two Paisley marriages of daughters of the late Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan; the inferred 25 August date and qualified profile comparisons are recorded in the linked family account. New original-checked Belfast News-Letter passages add a possible 1829 Belfast College student and probable Castledawson/India ministerial occurrences from 1836–1842; no middle name or kinship is established by them.

== Biography ==
Benjamin Glasgow, Esq., surgeon, formerly of Vera Cruz, Mexico, died in the prime of life at New Orleans on 26 November last, according to a notice published 20 May 1834. He was son of the late Mr Robert Glasgow of Cookstown, County Tyrone.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390554297/ Belfast News-Letter, 20 May 1834, p. 3, Benjamin Glasgow death notice], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref> A Dublin notice published 23 May repeats the surgeon, New Orleans and father details.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050049974/ Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 23 May 1834, p. 4, Benjamin Glasgow death notice], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The inferred death year is 1833. No age or mother is given. The documented father–son relationship is certain; profile identification remains on HOLD. Glasgow-3412 is a strong compatible candidate. The University of Glasgow index lists Benjamin Glasgow’s Master of Surgery in 1826, without father, birthplace or overseas details.<ref>[https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/people?search=&surname=Glas&forename=Benjamin University of Glasgow Story, Benjamin Glasgow, Master of Surgery, graduation 1826], official index checked 4 October 2026.</ref> This surgeon cannot be the mill Benjamin living in 1858/1870 or John’s merchant son living in 1856.

[[Glasgow-3412|Glasgow-3412]]: Live profile checked 4 October 2026: birth 1805 and surgery graduation 1826, no parents or death. The official University of Glasgow index independently confirms Benjamin Glasgow’s Master of Surgery in 1826, but gives no birth year/place, father or overseas career. Exact name, profession and chronology make a strong compatible candidate; the Cookstown/New Orleans bridge remains unproved.

Seek 1826 matriculation/degree papers with age, father or origin, and 1833 New Orleans death/burial or Vera Cruz medical records. Resolve identity before adding death or a father to Glasgow-3412.

Samuel-2054 and Samuel-1698 fit farmer/Cookstown comparisons; the regional Lisnagaver weaver Samuel-2908 is a weaker possibility, not a proved match. No family relationship is stated.

The Belfast College report dated 30 April 1831 names him in public mathematics examinations and, with Frederick Clarke, in the junior mathematical course and additional reading.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390545285/ Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1831, p.3, Belfast College report dated 30 April], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref>

A January 1837 report records his resignation as assistant in the Mathematical and Mercantile School of the Royal Belfast Institution. His class gave him Donnegan’s Greek Lexicon on 22 December 1836.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390542489/ Belfast News-Letter, 10 January 1837, p.2, resignation presentation on 22 December 1836], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref>

Rev. Adam D. Glasgow received a unanimous call to Berry Street Presbyterian Church, Belfast, in January 1840.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390553900/ Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1840, p.2, Berry Street ministerial call], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref> At a soiree on 5 March 1840 the congregation presented a pulpit dress to its newly ordained minister.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390555182/ Belfast News-Letter, 10 March 1840, p.2, Berry Street soiree on 5 March], original inspected 4 October 2026.</ref>

Marriage notice: on 25 July 1840 (reported as “25th ult.”), Mr James Small, of Lottery Cottage, county Armagh, married Miss Margaret Small of this town; the officiant was Rev. Adam Glasgow. Minister/officiant occurrence, not kinship. Keep adjacent London/St George’s wedding separate. Strongly compatible with Glasgow-1781, without unique identification. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390560450/ Belfast News-Letter, 7 August 1840, p. 3], original passage checked 5 October 2026.</ref>

Separate soirée passage: at a Tuesday-evening meeting on 27 October at the New School-house connected with the Presbyterian Church, Townsend-street, Rev. Adam Glasgow opened the proceedings; Rev. Josias Wilson closed with prayer. Do not replace/remove the existing Cookstown Academy/Robert Glasgow reading on this same page. Keep both distinct passages in one page row and one clip asset, with Adam as an additional excerpt. Strongly compatible with Glasgow-1781; no kinship. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563103/ Belfast News-Letter, 30 October 1840, p. 2], original passage checked 5 October 2026.</ref>

Belfast Town Mission annual meeting in the new school-room, Fisherwick-place, was held “on Wednesday evening last”; Rev. Adam Glasgow is among listed speakers. Preserve relative date wording; do not infer 28 October. Separate anti-slavery meeting on page is unrelated. Strongly compatible with Glasgow-1781; no kinship. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563260/ Belfast News-Letter, 6 November 1840, p. 2], original passage checked 5 October 2026.</ref>

General Synod report separately says ordained Ministers Messrs Adam Glasgow and James Carr offered themselves for foreign mission in India and were accepted; initial field Kathiawar/Guzerat, planned departure 4 August overland to Bombay. This is James Carr, not James Glasgow in adjacent set-apart report. Parent is coordinating separate passage with James packet; append distinct Adam target/excerpt if needed. Planned departure is not proof journey occurred. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390559244/ Belfast News-Letter, 14 July 1840, p. 1], original passage checked 5 October 2026.</ref>

== Biography ==

The Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser reported two marriages at Paisley on the 25th ult: George Sherbrooke Airey, Esq., a Royal Navy lieutenant and son of the late Lieutenant-General Sir George Airey, to Anne, second daughter of the late Robert Glasgow, Esq.; and, at the same time, Rev. George Drake, son of Rev. John Drake, rector of Stourton, to Charlotte Maria Cecilia, youngest daughter of the late Robert Glasgow, Esq., of Montgreenan, Ayr. The 25 August 1847 date is inferred from ‘25th ult’ relative to the 2 September issue. The clipped passage does not include the issue header. Profile matches remain qualified; the notice names no mothers or Irish origins.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/401331272/ Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 2 September 1847, p. 4, marriages], original passage visually checked; issue date and page verified separately.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The printed wording is evidence for the two marriages and the stated father relationships at the level of the people named in the notice. The date 25 August 1847 is inferred from ‘25th ult’; it is not printed as a full date. The clipped passage does not show the issue header.

Candidate comparisons remain qualified. Robertson-30564 is the probable late Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan candidate: the 1847 notice calls Charlotte the youngest daughter of the late Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan; the 1827 birth notice places an unnamed daughter of Mrs Robertson Glasgow at Rome; a profile-cited 1841 census transcription lists Robert Glasgow with Charlotte, age 10, though that census has not been independently checked. The existing Montgreenan succession account connects Robertson-30564 (Robert Robertson, later using Glasgow; died 1845) with the estate. This evidence supports the candidate beyond the current tree links, but does not prove the identity. Glasgow-1076 (1747–1827) remains a weaker possible alternative because his death before 1847 is compatible with “late”; no reviewed evidence definitively excludes him. Anne Glasgow-3000 is possible; Charlotte Glasgow-3003 is strongly compatible by names, current Drake surname and 1827 birth; Rev George Drake-13873 is probable by name/title and the existing spouse link. No compatible profile for George Sherbrooke Airey was located in the bounded local search.

The previous local Open-profile summaries showed these existing tree links as unknown (tree-only), with no evidence IDs: Robertson-30564 as father of Glasgow-3000 and Glasgow-3003 (generated claims with provenance wikitree_parent_field), and Drake-13873 as spouse of Glasgow-3003 (generated claim with provenance wikitree_spouse_field). Those prior assessments describe the state of the evidence before this notice; the tree links themselves are not documentary proof. The record-level father and spouse statements are direct, but their application to the profile candidates remains pending identity confirmation. No profile relationship upgrade is claimed or applied. No mother is named or assessed.

Next checks: independently identify George Sherbrooke Airey and verify the Anne and Charlotte candidate assignments using biographical, naval, clerical, baptismal or marriage records. Reassess candidate relationship status only after identity is established.

Inspect RS25 vols. 9/10, fols. 135/171, then compare the 1614 Inveresk entry and Alexander’s baptismal family. Keep Edward occurrences separate. [[Glasgow-994|Eduard, indexed in 1609 with father James]], and [[Glasgow-1558|Edward, baptised 1615]], are compatible alternatives to Edward-1557. No kinship is selected.

facts.finding: 6 February 1531/32: Costin Thomsone stands surety for Jhone Glasgw’s goods. The same court names Jhone of Glasgw among Upper Quothquan tenants who forcibly recovered seized property from the barony officer after he reached Libberton. == Biography ==
George Glasgw was named in Mureistoun in the Calder barony act dated 19 April 1586, ordering a muster on 4 August. The entry establishes an obligation, not attendance.<ref>James Maidment, ed., ''Analecta Scotica'', I (1834), article CXVI, pp.395–396,399; https://archive.org/details/analectascotica00maidgoog. Printed pages inspected 15 October 2026; manuscript not inspected.</ref> McCall’s 1894 parish history repeats the same occurrence, rather than providing a second record.<ref>H.B. McCall, ''History and Antiquities of the Parish of Mid-Calder'' (1894), p.16; https://archive.org/details/historyantiquiti00mcal.</ref>

An adult George Glasgow witnessed the Mid Calder baptism on 17 February 1605 of George, son of James Glasgow, whose residence is provisionally read Muirestoun, probably Murieston. John Smith was another witness; a final witness remains unresolved. The witness’s own residence and his relationship to the father and child are not stated.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Mid Calder Old Parish Registers, 694/1, volume 10, p.7, baptism 17 February 1605; https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/; original owner-held page re-inspected 16 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The 1586 man and 1605 witness are probably one person, as a working identity reviewed on 16 October 2026. The particular holding associated with the 1605 household, the local surname and a compatible 19-year adult career support that preference. The witness’s own residence is unstated; another George remains possible. The witness might be James’s father or another relative or neighbour; no parent relationship is selected. Birth date, parents, spouse, children and death are unknown. No live profile creation is recommended while compatible existing profiles are unresolved.

[[Glasgow-1099]] remains compatible with either adult occurrence but has no documented Mureistoun holding. [[Glasgow-3171]] is a very weak undated comparison requiring exceptional longevity; his 1676 burial gives no age. [[Glascoe-36]] remains compatible with the 1586 man, while the reported but unsupported 1589 death needs checking before using it to exclude the 1605 witness. [[Glasgow-1082]] is the child and cannot be either adult in this baptism.

Compare the other Mid Calder baptism pages for the same holding and witnesses, then inspect NLS MS.3724 and Beveridge’s transcript MS.3725 for George, James, heirs, leases and succession at Mureistoun. The catalogue places the 1586 land-title courts at original pp.1–15 and the chronological court sequence at pp.23–189; it records a gap between 2 May 1592 and 26 November 1594. These manuscript pages have not been read.<ref>National Library of Scotland, catalogue entries MS.3724, https://manuscripts.nls.uk/repositories/2/archival_objects/37880, and MS.3725, https://manuscripts.nls.uk/repositories/2/archival_objects/37881; catalogue consulted 15 October 2026, manuscript pages uninspected.</ref>
